doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Joining Basie and life on the bus
title: Arranging by humming: 'Every Tub' and 'Sent for You Yesterday'
summary: He explains that these Basie pieces were his head arrangements, worked out by humming parts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: After I had joined Basie. He wanted me to come back in the band and after I had made a few solos on the records with Basie, like, “Sent For You Yesterday,” that’s the first record I made with Basie, “Every Tub”…
Yeah, “Every Tub” and “Sent For You Yesterday”, those were my arrangements.
And how did you learn how to arrange, I mean you wrote out the parts?
I just wrote out the melody and I would hum what I would want everybody else to play, you know “Boop boo.”
